summary: reservation: estimate at typical output, not max
description:
Live testing surfaced the picker-vs-reservation gap I flagged in
PR #40 review:

  Picker says ~2 Anthropic queries per day (typical-output math).
  Reservation reserves at MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=8192 worst-case.
  → User does 1 Anthropic query (\$0.04 actual), tries Q2,
    reservation \$0.15 worst-case won't fit alongside \$0.04
    already used. 429.

Reality after fix (estimate at TYPICAL_OUTPUT_TOKENS=2000):
  Q1 reserve \$0.06; actual \$0.07 → usd_used 0.07.
  Q2 reserve \$0.06; 0.07+0.06=0.13 ≤ 0.1667 → allowed.
  Q3 attempt: 0.14+0.06=0.20 > 0.1667 → rejected.
  User gets 2 Anthropic queries — matches picker.

Files:
  - src/app/api/query/route.ts: change the computeCost estimate
    from MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS to TYPICAL_OUTPUT_TOKENS. Add import
    from pricing-config. Add a comment explaining the distinction
    between reservation estimate (typical-case budget reservation)
    and the API ceiling (max_tokens still passes 8192 to OpenRouter
    so verbose responses don't truncate).

Risk acknowledged: a single verbose query whose actual exceeds the
typical reservation will overshoot the cap. finalizeBudget records
the overage; subsequent reservations correctly reject. Operator
absorbs ~\$0.10 max per overshoot — bounded and small at pre-launch
scale.

Done when:
  - /api/query reservation uses TYPICAL_OUTPUT_TOKENS not MAX.
  - Tests + tsc + lint + build clean.
  - Live: a fresh pro user can run 2-3 Anthropic queries before
    cap rejects (matching picker label of ~2).

Spec: BRD-model-selection.md §6.2 + PR #40 review thread.

resolution.note: Reservation now estimates at TYPICAL_OUTPUT_TOKENS instead of MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS. Picker labels and actual reservation behavior now align — user gets the queries/day the picker shows. Verbose-response overshoot bounded and operator-absorbable at pre-launch scale. 247 tests pass; tsc + lint + build clean.
